quizDraft.title: Give nav links box behavior and turn content groups into cards
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The navigation links still behave like ordinary inline text, and the main sections/articles do not yet read as reusable content cards. Inline-block gives each nav link box behavior without forcing a new line, while box-model styling can turn the existing semantic content groups into distinct cards without wrappers. Add `display: inline-block;` to `nav a`. Then style the existing `main section, main article` boxes with `border: 1px solid #cbd5e1;`, `padding: 1.25rem;`, and `margin-block: 1rem;`. Preview the site: navigation should keep its inline flow, and existing sections/articles should gain consistent borders, inner space, and vertical separation.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Use the existing semantic elements; do not create decorative wrappers to get the card effect.

help.concept: Inline-block gives each nav link box behavior without forcing a new line, while box-model styling can turn the existing semantic content groups into distinct cards without wrappers.
help.hint_1: Use the existing semantic elements; do not create decorative wrappers to get the card effect.
help.hint_2: Preview the site: navigation should keep its inline flow, and existing sections/articles should gain consistent borders, inner space, and vertical separation.

quizDraft.title: Contain the wide table and the contact form
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The Projects table can be wider than its container, and the Contact form still spreads without a controlled visual box. Local horizontal `overflow` protects the page from a wide table, while `max-width`, `padding`, and a `border` give the existing form a readable contained measure. Add `table { display: block; overflow-x: auto; }`. Then give the existing form `max-width: 36rem;`, `padding: 1.5rem;`, and `border: 1px solid #cbd5e1;`. Check Projects and Contact: the table should scroll horizontally when needed, and the form should look like a deliberate bounded panel.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Keep `overflow` on the table itself, and size the existing form rather than changing its HTML.

help.concept: Local horizontal `overflow` protects the page from a wide table, while `max-width`, `padding`, and a `border` give the existing form a readable contained measure.
help.hint_1: Keep `overflow` on the table itself, and size the existing form rather than changing its HTML.
help.hint_2: Check Projects and Contact: the table should scroll horizontally when needed, and the form should look like a deliberate bounded panel.

quizDraft.title: Finish the Module 2 display and sizing checkpoint
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The Contact labels can still sit awkwardly beside controls, the table does not yet claim its available `width`, and the profile image has no block-level centering behavior. Block `display` gives labels and the image predictable box behavior, while a full-`width` table uses the available container before `overflow` becomes necessary. Add `form label { display: block; }`, then add `table { width: 100%; }` and refine `img` with `display: block;` and `margin-inline: auto;`. Preview Contact, Projects, and the profile image: labels should start their own lines, the table should fill its container, and the image should center as a block.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Use the elements already in the HTML; this is the final `display`/`overflow` cleanup before Flexbox.

help.concept: Block `display` gives labels and the image predictable box behavior, while a full-`width` table uses the available container before `overflow` becomes necessary.
help.hint_1: Use the elements already in the HTML; this is the final `display`/`overflow` cleanup before Flexbox.
help.hint_2: Preview Contact, Projects, and the profile image: labels should start their own lines, the table should fill its container, and the image should center as a block.
